abstract: Archaea and bacteria acquire resistance to viruses by integrating fragments of foreign DNA at the beginning of a CRISPR locus. In the archaeon Pyrococcus furiosus, histones bind the leader to promote specific integration at the first CRISPR repeat. However, it remains unknown whether archaeal CRISPR leaders contain conserved DNA sequence motifs required for integration. Here, we analyze 542 archaeal CRISPR leaders found across Thermococcales and Methanococcales. We identify 36 motifs found up to 500 bps upstream of archaeal CRISPR loci. Scrambling or truncating novel motifs or histone binding sites found 100-400 bps upstream of the P. furiosus CRISPR modestly decreases integration efficiency. However, mutation of motif T2, which overlaps with the proximal histone site and is adjacent to the CRISPR, ablates both histone-mediated and histone-independent integration. Mutations tiled across T2 reveal that a pyrimidine at position -3 of the leader is required for histone-independent integration, and basepairs -4 to -19 are required for histone-mediated integration. T2 is found in most Thermococcales, and a similar sequence is found in most Methanococcales leaders, suggesting this motif may be a broadly conserved element that facilitates CRISPR adaptive immunity across taxonomic orders. These data shed light on the sequence requirements for histone-mediated DNA integration.
